text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Bulgaria's Interior ministry said it had detained 450 luxury cars registered in the country after 1994 and valued at over 100,000 German marks each to check their origin in a bid to step up fight against trade in stolen cars and against corruption. @

-- Bulgaria's caretaker cabinet decided to cut by 20 percent the minimum prices of Bulgarian-made and imported cigarettes because of the stable lev/dollar exchange rate, the government press centre said.

-- Bulgaria's government said it had sacked the chairman of the government's Price Committee over incompetence and lack of cooperation between the committee and the cabinet in the price liberalisation process. @

-- Germany's Foreign minister Klaus Kinkel pledged support to the interim government's market reform efforts at a meeting with Bulgaria's President Petar Stoyanov during a stopover in the town of Plovdiv.

-- Bulgaria's state soda ash producer Sodi-Devnya, in which Belgium's Solvay SA chemical producer is expected to acquire a 60 percent stake after the sell-off is finalised, posted 7.15 billion levs pretax profit for 1996, Sodi officials said. @

-- The Bulgarian National Bank said it had allowed Bulgaria's state owned Bulbank, a co-operative union and a local wine maker to acquire up to 98 percent of Central Co-operative Bank's voting shares.
-- The Bulgarian National Bank said it had decided to open a bankruptcy procedure through the courts against the private Capitalbank after it ascertained Capitalbank's insolvency. @
-- Bulgaria hopes to sign a free trade accord ith Poland by mid-1997 in a bid to boost bilateral trade and help join the Central European Free Trade Agreement, a senior government official said.
-- Bulgaria's interim cabinet raised the minimum salary to 29,920 levs from 17,600 levs from April 1.
-- Bulgaria's caretaker government is expected to report to President Petar Stoyanov over its performance since taking office in mid-February. @
-- Bulgaria's Privatisation said it had chosen the Spanish-Bulgarian investment consortium Marbex Ltd as a buyer of a 70-percent stake of Bulgaria's Devnya Ziment cement plant for $44.5 million.

-- Bulgaria's interim cabinet sacked the board of directors of the National Electricity Company because it had not efficiently supported its proposal for a new rise of electricity and central heating prices, Prime minister Stefan Sofianski said. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
